newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds weaken under currency pressures.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds weaken under currency pressures.

text.p: Irish government bonds sank in active trade on Wednesday as prices were heavily influenced by developments in the Irish currency market, dealers said. In afternoon trading, the Irish pound hovered close to Tuesday's high at 2.4647 marks and slipped to 1.0118 stg.
"We have seen very active selling interest because sellers are cashing in on the high mark/Irish rate," one dealer said.
By 1516 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 had dropped 68p at 106.47 to yield 6.02 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down 82p at 107.30 to yield 6.83 percent.
"Markets like Italy and Spain don't seem to be doing that well and Ireland has followed that downward trend," the dealer added.
Dealers said UK gilt prices dropped sharply as the market squirmed under an unexpected fall in domestic employment, and a surprise pick-up in average earnings and PSBR data.
U.S. consumer prices data for September rose as expected by 0.3 percent month-on-month and markets shrugged off any post-data after-shocks, dealers said.
